q-36500.name: Question 1
q-36500.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
q-36500.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113557.problem:
$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=5{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}-{b}_{3}.$
q-113557.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $x=5{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}-{b}_{3},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-37150.name: Question 5
q-37150.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
q-37150.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 6-7\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}6 & -7 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -\frac{7}{3} \\ -1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].

$$

q-82605.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 5 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 5 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 8-5\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82711.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-82711.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-2\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82710.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-82710.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 11 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 11 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 3-11\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113615.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ relative to the basis $B.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} & -4 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$

\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -6 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
